title: fix(core): a date macro inside a longer string is a literal on the client too
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoH1SLb7yGpZj1NnaFvhbT6W)_
Fixes #35754

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 控制台里筛选值若只是「包含」日期宏的一段文字(例如 from {today} on),改前浏览器会把其中的宏换成日期,改后原样保留,与服务器的读法一致;整值为一个宏的写法照常解析。
- 属于筛选占位符契约一致性的收口:同一个筛选在控制台和服务器上应命中同一批记录。
- 只有把日期宏夹在长文本里当筛选值的作者会看到差异(以前也只在控制台生效、服务器不认),影响面小,可直接撤回本改动恢复旧行为。
- 无。

## What changes

The spec reads a filter value as a placeholder only when the value is ENTIRELY one wrapped token (`FILTER_TOKEN_WRAPPED_RE` in `@objectstack/spec/data`: "a value that merely CONTAINS braces (`'acme {x} deal'`) is untouched, as are `{a}{b}` and `{{x}}`"), and the server resolver `resolveFilterTokens` in `@objectstack/core` applies that reading. The client resolver did not: after its whole-value match, `resolveDateMacros` in `@object-ui/core` ran a second, global replace over the string, so `'from {today} on'` became `'from 2026-05-25 on'` in the console and stayed literal on the server. The card's question (which side is the contract) is answered by the spec text above, so the client aligns with it.

- `resolveDateMacros` (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts`): the global pass is removed. A string resolves only when it is one whole `{token}` / `${token}`; anything else is returned as written. The header says so and names the spec reading.
- `substituteTokens` in `ui/packages/core/src/utils/compare-to.ts` (the previous-period token rename behind `shiftFilterByCompareTo`) had the same embedded pass. With the resolver fixed alone, `'from {today} on'` would have been renamed to `'from {yesterday} on'` and then kept literal, so the comparison query would have filtered on a different literal from the current one. It now renames only whole-value tokens, through the file's existing `wholeToken` helper. Same defect class, mechanical, no other claim on the file, same test family: fixed here under the bounded in-place rule and declared in the report.

**Caller census** (every non-test caller of `resolveDateMacros` at base `8145424b`; none relies on the embedded form):

| Caller | What it passes | Effect |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `resolveFilterPlaceholders` (core `filter-tokens.ts`), and through it every list, grid, chart, dashboard and detail surface | filter trees | the fix itself |
| `shiftFilterByCompareTo` / `lastPeriodBefore` (core `compare-to.ts`) | filter trees; `lastPeriodBefore` builds a whole `{last_UNIT_start}` | aligned (see above); `lastPeriodBefore` unchanged |
| `isUsableDateString` (core `dashboard-filters.ts`) | a dashboard date-filter value | an embedded macro no longer counts as a usable date; it never reached the server as one |
| `resolveInitialDateMacro` (plugin-calendar `initialDate.ts`) | `calendar.initialDate`, which the spec defines as a wrapped token | same outcome: an embedded string already resolved to a non-date and fell back to today |
| plugin-dashboard `utils.ts` | re-export only | none |

The card's "page/URL params" hypothesis does not hold: `resolveParam` inside `resolveDateMacros` is the parameterised date-macro grammar (`{N_days_ago}` and friends), which the server also resolves (`parseDateMacroParam`), not page or URL parameters. No dashboard title or URL template calls this resolver.

## Tests

- New pin `ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/date-macros.embeddedLiteral-35754.test.ts`: an embedded fixed macro, an embedded parameterised macro, an embedded macro beside a whole one in a filter tree (through `resolveFilterPlaceholders`), a previous-period comparison, and `{{today}}` all stay literal. CONTROLS: a whole `{today}`, `${today}` and `{7_days_ago}` still resolve; `'acme {x} deal'` and `{a}{b}` are untouched.
- **Pin flip (deviation):** `date-macros.test.ts` pinned the embedded behaviour in two assertions: "leaves unknown tokens untouched and ignores non-strings" expected `'hello {today} world'` to become `'hello 2026-05-25 world'`, and "accepts both {token} and ${token} forms" expected `'range: ${last_week_start}..${today}'` to become `'range: 2026-05-18..2026-05-25'`. Both now expect the value as written; the whole-value `'${today}'` assertion beside them is unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- Not filed: the hotcrm reconciliation harness keeps its own date-macro resolver (`scripts/analytics-reconcile/macros.ts`); read at hotcrm `e7fe77f`, it has no global replace pass, so nothing there disagrees.
- The client whole-value grammar stays the token-NAME grammar (`[a-zA-Z0-9_]+`), narrower than the server's recognition grammar. That is a separate question (what an unknown wrapped value does on the client) and is not touched here.
